lyrics:
[Intro: laughter, running footsteps, piano slide, stomping beat]
Alright, listen up

[Verse 1: chanted lead, the group shouts the answers]
Before you get a yes, there's a panel, there's a test
(Who's on it?) Five of my best
(What's the question?) Can you hang, can you laugh
Can you handle all the screenshots in the group chat?

[Chorus: all five in unison, handclaps]
You like me? Cute. Run it by the group chat
Love's a team sport, baby, that's a fact
If they say "who's this?" then you won't last
Gotta run it, run it, run it by the group chat
Give me that shoobie-zap, shoobie-zap-zoo

[Verse 2: second chanted lead, the group answers]
You can bring the flowers, you can bring the car
(Does he listen?) That's the bar
(Does she show up?) Rain or shine
If you're good to my people then you're good to mine

[Chorus: all five in unison, handclaps]
You like me? Cute. Run it by the group chat
Love's a team sport, baby, that's a fact
If they say "who's this?" then you won't last
Gotta run it, run it, run it by the group chat
Give me that shoobie-zap, shoobie-zap-zoo

[Bridge: roll call rap, each voice takes a line]
We got Priya with receipts, we got Jo who never sleeps
We got Dee who reads your stars, Kay who checks your car
And Nan's eighty-three and she's meaner than me
So mind your manners when you come for tea

[Breakdown: sung softly, piano and finger snaps]
Lovers come and lovers go
These five were here before hello

[Final Chorus: everyone shouting, key hits, whistles]
You like me? Cute. Run it by the group chat
Love's a team sport, baby, that's a fact
If they say "who's this?" then you won't last
Gotta run it, run it, run it by the group chat
Give me that shoobie-zap, shoobie-zap-zoo
Shoobie-zap, shoobie-zap-zoo

[Outro: laughter, one voice, door slam]
Approved. For now.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 110 BPM, 4/4, B major. A stomping, bouncing pop-rap strut. Loud, cheeky and fast-moving.

VOICE: Five distinct female voices: one husky, one sweet, one loud and brash, one cool, one soulful. Verses are chanted, half rapped, with the others shouting replies. Choruses are unison shouts, not polished harmony. Laughter and ad-libs are left in.

INSTRUMENTS: A stomping kick and clap pattern. Bright pub-style piano chords and slides. A rubbery, funky bass line. Scratchy wah guitar. Synth horn stabs. Finger snaps and a soft electric piano in the breakdown. Sound effects: footsteps, laughter, a door.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, laughter and footsteps, a piano slide, the beat. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:28 Chorus 1. 0:50 Verse 2. 1:08 Chorus 2. 1:30 Bridge, a roll-call with each voice taking a line. 1:48 Breakdown, two soft sung lines over piano and snaps. 2:02 Final chorus, everyone shouting, last line doubled. 2:36 Outro, a laugh, one spoken line, a door slam at 2:50.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-90s British pop: dry, bright and busy, voices loud and slightly rough, nothing over-tuned.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The nonsense line at the end of each chorus, shouted by all five.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The friends have a group chat and one of them is eighty-three. The song works for a girl gang at twenty and for the same women decades later.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Mischief throughout, with two lines of real loyalty in the breakdown.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

Before anyone gets a yes, they have to get past her friends, who are already discussing it.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: friends in their twenties, or the same friends at forty-five vetting second marriages; a family with opinions; a band; or your own conscience, which also has a group chat.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: friendship as the rule, chanted call-and-response verses, a roll-call, and a nonsense phrase in the hook. Designed mishearing: 'shoobie-zap' has no meaning on purpose, and 'run it by the group chat' is heard as 'run it by the cool cat'.
